fixes.why: The first four examples are people ascribing glory to the LORD or God. But the row also holds glory given BY someone TO someone: John 17:22 ('I have given them the glory You gave Me'), Luke 4:6 (the devil offering 'all their glory'), 1 Pet 1:21 (God raising Christ and glorifying Him), Ps 84:11 ('the LORD gives grace and glory') and Isa 35:2 ('the glory of Lebanon will be given to it'). Those are a different action from ascribing glory. They also keep John 17:22 in the same row as Isa 42:12 and Ps 115:1, which were meant to be heard on their own terms: moving Isa 42:8 and 48:11 out did not finish the job, because Isa 42:12 and Ps 115:1 are in both row 10 and this row, with John 17:22 beside them.
fixes.fix: Take Isa 42:12 and Ps 115:1 out of this row (they stay in the Hebrew-only row). Move John 17:22, Luke 4:6, 1 Pet 1:21, Ps 84:11 and Isa 35:2 to their own row, 'Glory given: the glory You gave Me; 'I can give it to anyone I wish'; 'the LORD gives grace and glory'', or at least relabel this row 'Give glory (to God), ascribe glory' and put those five in a separate labelled row. John 17:22 should not share a row with any Isaiah or Psalm verse.

fixes.row: “I will not yield My glory to another”; glory given to the LORD alone
fixes.why: Hebrew-only and separate from John 17:22: the rabbi seat accepts the row, and it is the right home for Isa 42:8 and 48:11. But 'alone' is not in Isa 42:12 ('Let them give glory to the LORD') and not in Ps 115:1 ('not to us ... but to Your name'). The label says more than two of its four verses say, and 'alone' also leans toward the exclusivity reading that the page elsewhere declines to draw.
fixes.fix: Relabel: '“I will not yield My glory to another”; “give glory to the LORD”; “not to us, O LORD, but to Your name be the glory”' (the text's own phrases, no 'alone').

fixes.why: This verb catch-all has no note, yet its first two examples are Rom 8:30 ('those He predestined ... He also glorified') and Acts 13:48 ('all who were appointed for eternal life believed'), the two verses on which traditions most sharply part on election. The election note sits only on the noun row 'Suffering and glory; called to glory'; the worker's report assumes it covers the verb too and it does not. The same row holds 2 Cor 3:10 ('what was once glorious has no glory now'), which carries the Law/Israel note in the noun catch-all but none here.
fixes.fix: Add a note to the verb 'Every other use': 'Among them Rom 8:30 and Acts 13:48, which speak of those predestined, called and appointed; Christian traditions part on who is meant and on what that rests, and the page takes no side. And 2 Cor 3:10, which sets the two ministries side by side as the text has them (see the note at the noun row 'Every other use'); the page does not say what this implies for the Law or for Israel.' Alternatively move Rom 8:30 and Acts 13:48 into a labelled verb row under the same note.

fixes.why: Fair as worded, and it names the passage. Two weaknesses. (1) It is one note in a 29-verse bin whose four visible examples are Exod 29:43, Mark 10:37, 1 Pet 5:4 and 1 Tim 1:11, none of them 2 Cor 3, so a Jewish reader who looks for the passage under a label finds a bin called 'Every other use'. (2) The note says '2 Cor 3:7-11' but 3:8 is not in this row (it is in the Holy Spirit row), and the note omits the context the text itself supplies: 3:7 is about Moses' face, told at Exod 34:29-35.
fixes.fix: Reword the note: '2 Cor 3:7, 9, 10, 11 (and 3:8, listed under the Holy Spirit) set the glory of Moses' ministry, whose face the Israelites could not gaze at (Exodus 34:29-35), beside the glory of the ministry of the Spirit and of righteousness, as the text has them; the page does not say what this implies for the Law or for Israel, and readers part on that.' If the panel would rather the passage be findable, a labelled row 'Moses' face and the two ministries (2 Cor 3)' holding 3:7, 3:9-11 under the same note is acceptable and no less neutral than a bin.

fixes.row: Where the English does not say glory: honor, wealth, riches, splendor, pomp, praise
fixes.why: One row is not honest here; it should be two (indeed three kinds are in it). Kind 1 (about 45 verses: Prov 3:16, 8:18, 22:4, 1 Chr 29:12, 2 Chr 1:11-12, and so on) is the Hebrew word in a DIFFERENT SENSE (honor, wealth, riches, 'weight'), and the row's job is to show that this is not the glory-sense. Kind 2 (Isa 8:7, 10:16, 10:18, 16:14, 17:3-4, Gen 45:13, Job 19:9, 1 Cor 15:40-41, John 12:43, 1 Thess 2:6, Luke 14:10) is the SAME glory-sense that the Berean renders 'splendor', 'pomp' or 'praise', so these belong WITH glory, not apart from it. Putting both under 'Where the English does not say glory' says to the reader that all 63 are alike, when the first group is 'not glory' and the second is 'glory by another name'. All four examples are kind 1, so the note's second kind is invisible. Kind 3 (Ps 16:9, 30:12, 108:1 'heart/tongue/soul', Ps 57:8 'my glory', Gen 49:6, Ps 4:2 'my honor') is the Hebrew word standing for the self, and Ps 57:8 actually prints 'glory' in the Berean, contradicting the label. The examples carry no original word (words are empty), so nothing on the card says which Hebrew or Greek word these verses rest on. Isa 16:14, 17:4 and John 12:43 are also in 'People and their glory'.
fixes.fix: Split in two: (A) 'Honor, wealth, riches: the same Hebrew word in another sense' (kind 1; eg Prov 3:16, 8:18, 22:4, 1 Chr 29:12); note: 'The Hebrew כָּבוֹד (from 'be heavy') is also rendered honor, wealth and riches; these are not the glory of God, listed so the word's other uses are seen.' (B) 'Where the Berean prints splendor, pomp or praise, or 'my glory' for oneself, and the original word is the one glossed glory' (kind 2 plus kind 3, including Ps 57:8, Ps 16:9, 30:12, 108:1, Acts 22:11 'brilliance'); note: 'Here the original word is the glory word; the English chose another.' Remove Isa 16:14, 17:4 and John 12:43 from (B) or from 'People and their glory' so no verse sits in both. Wherever the builder allows it, show the original word on the card of each picked verse.

fixes.row: People and their glory: kings, nations, a land; glory sought, received from people; one called another's glory
fixes.why: The verses are included correctly and stand true to the text (11:7 says man is 'the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man'; 11:15 says 'if a woman has long hair, it is her glory'). The note is the weak point. 'What 1 Cor 11:7 and 11:15 say of man and woman' mislabels 11:15, which speaks of hair, not of man and woman, and it does not tell the reader what either verse says. A reader sees 'the woman is the glory of man' in a row of Moab's splendor and Jacob's splendor with no word saying that the same verse calls man 'the glory of God', and 11:15's hair (a culturally loaded subject) is reduced to a bare reference. It also frames the divide as complementarian against egalitarian, which is American shorthand.
fixes.fix: Reword the note: '1 Cor 11:7 says the man is the image and glory of God and the woman is the glory of man; 11:15 says a woman's long hair is her glory. The page gives the verses as written and takes no side on how they apply.' Do not name complementarian or egalitarian positions. Keep 1 Cor 11:7 in the 'glory of God' row as well, as it is.

fixes.row: People and their glory: kings, nations, a land; ...
fixes.why: Three of the four examples (Isa 16:14 'splendor', Isa 17:4 'splendor', John 12:43 'praise') do not show the word 'glory' that the label uses; only 1 Cor 11:7 does. The original-word chip is shown, but rule 6 asks for the example to show its label, and a reader scanning English will think the row is mis-filed.
fixes.fix: Reorder the picks so the first four shown say 'glory' in the Berean (for example Matt 6:29, Luke 2:32, Rom 9:4 or Luke 12:27, with 1 Cor 11:7 kept among them), leaving the 'splendor' and 'praise' verses further down the row or, per the split above, in the splendor/pomp row.

fixes.why: The row's own note says it holds 'the verses where the text itself names Christ, Jesus, the Son of Man or the Lamb beside glory', and Matt 16:27, Mark 8:38, 2 Pet 1:17 and Phil 2:11 are in both person rows because they name both. But Rom 6:4 ('just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father') and Jas 2:1 ('our glorious Lord Jesus Christ') name Christ plainly beside glory and are not in the Christ row (Rom 6:4 is only in the Father row, Jas 2:1 only in the titles row). Rom 6:4 being in the Father row and not the Christ row is inconsistent with the rule applied elsewhere, and a reader who counts will see the Christ row as incomplete.
fixes.fix: Add Rom 6:4 and Jas 2:1 (and Eph 1:17, which names 'the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory') to the Christ row, keeping them in the Father row and titles row as they are. The picks are by hand, so the person rows must be read against each other once.

fixes.row: Suffering and glory; called to glory; the body raised in glory
fixes.why: The note says 'the label uses only the text's own verbs and nouns', but Rom 9:23 says 'prepared in advance for glory' and 1 Cor 2:7 'God predestined for our glory', not 'called'. Filing them under 'called to glory' is not what they say, and it quietly hides the verses the note is warning about. The note is good on its own terms; the label is not.
fixes.fix: Relabel: 'Suffering and glory; called, prepared in advance, brought to glory; the body raised in glory'. Keep the note unchanged (Christian traditions part on who is meant; the page takes no side).

fixes.row: Glorify the LORD, the LORD gains glory (Hebrew כָּבֵד)
fixes.why: Two of the four examples (Ps 22:23 'honor Him', Isa 25:3 'honor You') print 'honor', not 'glorify'. The Hebrew verb is the same one, but the label only has 'glorify', so the example does not show the label's word. The Hebrew verb is also the one in 'Honor your father', which the row rightly excludes.
fixes.fix: Relabel: 'Glorify or honor the LORD, the LORD gains glory (Hebrew כָּבֵד, sometimes printed honor)'.

fixes.row: The Holy Spirit named with glory
fixes.why: The row has no note, while the Father and Christ rows both say how the text relates them and that the page does not choose. Its first example is 2 Cor 3:18, 'the Lord, who is the Spirit', which is also in the 'Lord' title row where the note says readers take 'the Lord' of Father or Christ. A reader of the Spirit row sees the Spirit identified with the Lord there, with no sentence saying the page leaves that to the text. 1 Pet 1:11 is 'the Spirit of Christ' and Eph 3:16 'His Spirit', both of which relate the Spirit to another person.
fixes.fix: Add a note in the same form as the other two: 'The verses where the text itself names the Spirit, or the Spirit of Christ or of glory, beside glory. How it relates them is in the verses, and the page does not choose.'

worker_points.point: 1. Rows 4, 5, 6 (the persons); Lamb's doxologies Rev 5:12-13 in the Christ row
worker_points.why: Rev 5:12-13 in the Christ row is right: the verses say 'the Lamb'. The inconsistency is the reverse: Rom 6:4, Jas 2:1 and Eph 1:17 name Christ but are absent from the Christ row (see fixes). The Spirit row also needs a note.

worker_points.point: 2. Rows 10 and 11, Isaiah on its own; John 17:22
worker_points.why: The rabbi seat accepts the Hebrew-only row (Isa 42:8, 48:11, 42:12, Ps 115:1). But John 17:22 still sits in 'Give glory, ascribe glory' with Isa 42:12 and Ps 115:1 listed there too, so it still frames them; and 'alone' in the row-10 label goes beyond Isa 42:12 and Ps 115:1. Whether the two rows being apart is itself a reading: no, because the row is Hebrew-only by word, not by argument.
The no-choice notes are fair; Heb 13:21 and 1 Pet 4:11 are rightly left as 'Him'/'whom'; 2 Pet 3:18 sits in the Christ row because it names Christ in the verse. (Spirit row note is a separate fix.)

The verse says 'He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine'; the verse before names the Spirit of truth; the note says so and no more. John 16:14 is correctly under 'Jesus glorified' because Jesus is the one glorified. It is not a person-by-rule assignment.

The noun row's note is good, but the verb 'Every other use' holding Rom 8:30 and Acts 13:48 has no note, and the label 'called to glory' does not match Rom 9:23 ('prepared in advance') or 1 Cor 2:7 ('predestined'). No side is taken by the verses; only the note and label are missing.

The note is fair to Jewish readers in its wording but is a single sentence in a 29-verse bin, omits that 3:8 sits elsewhere, omits Exod 34:29-35 which 3:7 refers to, and is missing from the verb row that holds 3:10. Acceptable once these are added.
The verses stay, as the text has them. The note should say what each verse says (including that man is also 'the glory of God' and that 11:15 is about hair) and should not name a modern debate.

worker_points.point: 8. Rows 7 and 8 (appears, fills; Orthodox light, Jewish kavod)
worker_points.why: The rows state only what the verses say (appears, fills, departs, returns). The Ezekiel 9-11 and 43-44 verses are left without a reading of whether the glory is God or God's presence, which is right. Luke 2:14 and 19:38 ('glory in the highest') under 'above the heavens' are slightly loose but not misleading.
The label does not say whose glory and the Berean capitalises it in Ps 106:20, Jer 2:11 and Hos 4:7; Rom 1:23 is explicit. A rabbi hears the verses on their own terms.

worker_points.point: 10. Row 19, the merged other-sense row (one row or two)
worker_points.why: Two rows, because one group is the word in another sense (not glory) and the other is the glory-sense under a different English word (glory, by another name). One row with a note makes them look the same and hides the second kind, and Ps 57:8 prints 'glory' against the label. See the split fix.

worker_points.point: 11. Row 12 (doxologies plus purpose clauses; Rev 5:13 also in the Christ row)
worker_points.why: Both are 'to God / to the glory of God'; Rev 5:13 addresses God and the Lamb and is rightly in both rows.

missing.what: The account the 2 Cor 3 note depends on: the Hebrew Scriptures heard on their own terms for Moses' face (cross-reference in the note rather than a new row; the word kavod does not appear there, so it is context, not a glory verse)

1 Tim 3:16 ('taken up in glory') and 1 Pet 1:21 ('raised Him ... and glorified Him') speak of Christ but are in the catch-all or the 'give glory' row; a reader looking for Christ and glory will not find them under 'Christ named with glory' (the row's rule is that the verse names him; these two name him by 'He'/'Him' only, so leave out unless the rule is widened)

John 1:14 and Exod 33:18-22 are in the 'appears' row, but there is no row for the glory that is seen and cannot be seen ('no one may see Me and live'); an honest hub of the glory seen should hold both sides

summary: The hub is built with care and nearly all of it is true to the text, and the rabbi seat accepts the Hebrew-only Isaiah row, but it needs fixes before it ships: John 17:22 still shares a row with Isa 42:12 and Ps 115:1, the merged 'English does not say glory' row should be split in two, and the election and 2 Cor 3 notes are missing from the verb row. The Christ row lacks Rom 6:4 and Jas 2:1, the 1 Cor 11 note should say what the verses say, and a few labels (alone, called, honor) say more or less than their verses.
